Anya: Heads up — seeing repeated SLO misses on text-gen p99 in eu-west since 04:10 UTC. Correlates with sustained prefill queue and max-batch hits on older A10 pool.
Max: What's the error breakdown? logs/dash?
Anya: Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/reports/queueing-eu-west (private). p50 stable, p95 rising ~200ms, p99 +1.2s. Admission events show continuous `max_batch_reached` on eu-a10-old nodes.
Lucas: Those nodes are configured with max_batch=48 because of memory constraints; eu-new (V100/A100 equiv) runs 128. Router packing across both pools causes small requests to wait for big ones.
Olivia: We're also seeing KV prefill spikes — long context prefill (>=1024) holds the batch head for multiple steps, blocking other inflight tiny requests.
Anya: Repro: run mixed workload (16 tok and 1024 tok) against the eu endpoint -> queue grows, admission backpressure increases, more `max_batch_reached` events, and latency tail balloons.
Raj: Note: the enterprise routing policy for eu pins some customers to the older pool (security/latency preference). That combined with the mixed token distribution is the trigger.
Max: Quick mitigation options: 1) route small-token traffic off the old pool, 2) temporarily boost priority for <=64 token requests, 3) reduce max_batch on old pool (but that hurts throughput). Thoughts?
Lucas: Boosting small-req priority should reduce P99 quickly but will increase fragmentation and reduce cost efficiency. Lowering max_batch on old nodes is a blunt instrument — it stops head-of-line blocking but lowers utilization.
Anya: Proposed immediate actions (short window):
  - Apply routing override: send tokens<=64 to eu-new pool (30m)
  - Enable `small-req-priority` admission rule across eu region
  - Trigger scale-up policy for eu-a10-old if prefill queue > 80% for 5m
Olivia: Quick admission rule to try (will push as change):
```
admission_rules:
  - match: tokens <= 64
    action: priority_boost
    weight: 2
```
Raj: PR created for routing override (rollout: 10% -> 100% over 5m). Monitoring hooks added. @sre-oncall-bot will page if p99>500ms.
sre-oncall-bot: paging on-call (Rachel) — p99 latency in eu-west crossed 500ms (current 810ms)
Rachel: investigating node-level metrics now, checking GPU utilization, mem pressure, and prefill queue on eu-a10-old hosts 10.3.5.12-16.
Rachel: Node metrics show sustained GPU mem pressure and high kv-prefill latency on those hosts; one host repeatedly hitting out-of-memory evictions for KV cache.
Anya: After routing override (~+6m) p99 dropped to ~220ms and admission events reduced. Keeping override for 30m while we validate.
Lucas: Longer term we need: per-pool dynamic `max_batch` estimator based on observed token distribution & KV prefill cost; route-by-expected-token-distribution; avoid pinning large enterprise cohorts to legacy hardware. Add to roadmap.
Olivia: I'll open an RFC for dynamic max_batch + routing heuristics and include evaluation criteria (p99 improvement, cost delta, utilization).
Anya: Great. I'll jot down the immediate runbook steps and link to the incident board. Thanks all :thumbsup:
